title: assert_dev_ci_grants: optional hardening (delimiter-safe boundary, umask, role interpolation)
body:
Low-severity hardening from the F1-S8 #57 security review (core boundary VERIFIED SAFE — these are optional, non-blocking):

- **L1 (delimiter confusion):** `is_allowed_grant` uses `name.startswith(f"{allowed_database}.")`. A DB created as `"ROASTPILOT_DEV.evil"` (a name literally containing a dot) could false-match IF SHOW GRANTS renders a nested object unquoted. Exotic + already mitigated (the trailing-dot test rejects ROASTPILOT_DEV_EVIL; the SHOW DATABASES visibility check independently flags out-of-bounds DBs). Optional fix: reject any `name` containing a quote char, or split on `.` and compare the first component exactly.
- **L2 (dead defense):** `umask 077` is set AFTER `mktemp` (which already creates 0600), so it has no effect. No exposure (perms are 0600 throughout). Move umask above mktemp if kept, or drop it.
- **L3 (informational):** role name (vars.SNOWFLAKE_DEV_ROLE) is f-string-interpolated into `SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE {role}`. Operator-controlled repo var, not PR-controllable, connector doesn't multi-statement — not exploitable in the current threat model; noted for completeness.

Refs #11 (F1-S8). Do when convenient; the boundary is safe as-is.
